claims.statement: MelodyDatabase is the single Room database (file `melody.db`, version 10, `exportSchema = true`) exposing one DAO (`MelodyDao`); `DatabaseModule` builds it as a Hilt `@Singleton` via `Room.databaseBuilder` with all migrations v1→v10 registered through `addMigrations`.

Room v10 contains exactly 13 entity tables: songs (library master with unique `uri` index), playlists, playlist_song_cross_ref (order-preserving many-to-many), play_stats, playback_events (per-session rows for day/week/month aggregation), quick_skip_songs, quick_skip_short_play_counts, song_group_overrides, migration_state, artists, albums, song_artist_cross_ref, and song_emotions (per-window V/A curve plus user calibration fields).

Room entities declare no foreign-key constraints; all relationships (playlist↔song, song↔artist/album, songId-keyed stat rows) are logical and maintained by repository code — `MelodyDao.syncLibraryCatalog` rebuilds artist/album catalogs, song-artist refs, and the `songs.albumId` backfill idempotently, then deletes orphans.

MusicRepository persists the library as asynchronous full-table snapshots: changes are queued on a single-threaded IO scope (`Dispatchers.IO.limitedParallelism(1)`) that guarantees later snapshots supersede earlier ones, and `RoomMusicLibraryDataSource.persistSongs/persistPlaylists` replace whole tables inside `@Transaction` methods `replaceSongs`/`replacePlaylists` so main-thread UI actions never block on disk.

The composite index `(startedAtMs, isEffectivePlay, songId)` on `playback_events` covers all time-range aggregation queries (total duration, distinct songs, per-day durations, effective-play song TOP chart); migration 7→8 dropped the redundant single-column `startedAtMs` index from migration 5→6 and repaired fresh installs that lacked any index.

The mandatory Room schema-change workflow is: change entity/DAO → bump `MelodyDatabase` version → build `:data` (KSP `room.schemaLocation = $projectDir/schemas`) so the new JSON is exported to `data/schemas/cn.com.dcsgo.mihx.data.local.MelodyDatabase/` → register a `Migration(N, N+1)` in `DatabaseModule.addMigrations` → add a focused unit test for migrations with complex data movement; existing schema JSON files are immutable snapshots and must never be edited.

`verifyProductArchitecture` (root `build.gradle.kts`) machine-enforces persistence invariants: schema v1 must not contain `quick_skip_short_play_counts`, v2 must contain it but not `lrcUri`, v3 must contain `lrcUri` (making version history tamper-evident), `DatabaseModule` must keep the `Migration(1, 2)`/`Migration(2, 3)` registrations, and schema history must include versions 1–3; it also checks both backup rule files against the required privacy exclude list.

Migration history v1→v10: 1→2 create `quick_skip_short_play_counts`; 2→3 add `lrcUri`; 3→4 add `album`; 4→5 create `artists`/`albums`/`song_artist_cross_ref` + `songs.albumId`; 5→6 create `playback_events` with a `startedAtMs` index; 6→7 add `durationMs`; 7→8 swap to the composite index; 8→9 create `song_emotions`; 9→10 add `embeddingB64`/`userValence`/`userArousal`/`userTags` to `song_emotions` for the personalization loop.

`SharedPreferencesLegacyJsonMigration` performs the one-shot read-only migration of v1 SharedPreferences JSON into Room: it reads `music_player_prefs` (`songs_json`, `playlists_json`), `play_stats_prefs` (prefixed count/duration keys), and `quick_skip_songs_prefs`, upserts the parsed snapshot via `MelodyDao`, and is the only reason legacy SharedPreferences readers are retained.

Legacy migration idempotency is enforced by a `migration_state` marker row: `migrateIfNeeded()` short-circuits when `MigrationStateEntity("shared_preferences_json_v1", completedAt)` exists, and writes the marker only after the data upserts complete.

`LegacyJsonSnapshotParser` isolates parse failures per JSON block (`runCatching` per section, degrading to empty without blocking the others), deduplicates songs by `uri`, and filters playlist song references to ids that exist among successfully parsed songs; a test locks down that corrupt JSON still migrates stats and writes the completion marker.

The legacy migration trigger point is `MusicRepository.loadPersistedSongs()`, which runs `migrateIfNeeded()` before restoring from Room — after the one-shot migration Room is the single source of truth and legacy JSON is never consulted again.

The `player_settings` DataStore (owned by `PlayerSettingsRepository` via `PlayerSettingsKeys`) persists theme mode/variant, uniform-random, Bluetooth monitoring, playback notification, lyric font scale, sleep timer end time + play-last-song, daily listening goal, emotion-scan pause, the mood time-slot master switch (`mood_time_slot_enabled`), and local-music sort mode/direction; `DataStoreModule` provides it plus the legacy `music_player_prefs` SharedPreferences behind Hilt qualifiers.

Player settings reads carry a legacy SharedPreferences fallback and the write path deletes the legacy key: when DataStore lacks a value the legacy `dark_theme`-style key is consulted, and an explicit write (e.g. `setThemeMode`) both writes DataStore and removes the legacy key, so legacy values decay with use.
The sleep timer's end timestamp and play-last-song flag are persisted so `PlayerSleepTimerCoordinator.restore()` resurrects an unexpired countdown after app restart, resetting expired timers to zero.

`PlaybackStateStore` (in `:player`, implementing both `PlaybackStateStorage` and `PlaybackStateRepository`) owns the `playback_state` DataStore with keys `play_queue_json`, `play_position_ms`, `is_infinite_play`, `infinite_played_ids`, `current_song_id`; it is the process-death recovery snapshot for the Media3 session and is wired through `app/di/PlayerModule`.

Playback snapshot save semantics: an empty session (empty queue, no currentSongId, not infinite play) skips the write but deliberately keeps any existing snapshot — the UI-recreation window produces transient all-empty states and the old clear-on-empty behavior erased a valid 5s-old snapshot leaving the queue permanently empty after restart (2026-09-03 regression); explicit clearing goes through `clear()`; save failures are logged and swallowed so playback control is never interrupted.

`PlaybackStateSnapshotSerializer` encodes the queue as `{songIds, currentIndex, playMode, playOrderIds}` JSON preserving duplicates; decoding filters song ids against the current library, clamps `currentIndex`, repairs the play order against matched ids, and returns null on corrupt JSON or a missing `currentIndex` (a missing `playMode` defaults to `PlayMode.DEFAULT`); infinite-play played ids are likewise filtered to available songs.

Restore is a two-phase decision that removes the controller race: `PlayerPersistenceGraph` reads/decodes the snapshot on an IO coroutine in parallel with controller connection, then waits for `controllerReady` before consulting `hasLiveSession()` — a live session receives only the UI queue shadow backfill (never controller overwrite), while a cold start fully restores UI plus controller queue without autoplay; `restore` also re-anchors the queue onto the stored `current_song_id`, synthesizing a single-song queue if the song was not in the saved queue.

Snapshot writes have two safety nets: `PlayerPlaybackStateAutosaver` saves every 5 seconds (`DEFAULT_INTERVAL_MS = 5_000L`) on playback position, and `AppMediaSessionService.onDestroy`/`onTaskRemoved` write the final snapshot via the suspend `persistCurrentPlaybackSnapshot` on a process-level `@ApplicationScope` coroutine (ExoPlayer state must be read on the calling thread; only the disk write is async) and settle the playlist resume record in the same coroutine.

`PlaylistResumeDataStore` (the `playlist_resume` DataStore) keeps one `resume_<playlistId>` key holding `{"songId":N,"updatedAtMs":T}` JSON plus a `source_playlist_id` marker for the queue's source playlist; `switchSourcePlaylist` and `recordCurrentSource` must read-and-write inside a single `edit` transaction, otherwise rapid source switching can settle a song onto the wrong playlist.

`PlaylistResumeDataStoreTest` locks down the transactional semantics (switching settles the old source playlist with the current song, same-source switch does not settle, switching to non-playlist source settles then clears, `recordCurrentSource` returns whether a record was made) and that corrupt resume JSON observes as null.

`TimeSlotConfigStore` (the `mood_time_slot` DataStore) stores all mood time-slot configs in the single key `time_slot_configs` as a JSONArray of `{id, name, start, end, tags}` — chosen over Room because the config count is single-digit to low-double-digit; `save` validates via `MoodSlotResolver.validate` (name/tags/zero-length/overlap) and throws `IllegalArgumentException` carrying the conflicting slot's name, rewriting the whole key sorted by start time.

Time-slot config parsing is two-level fault tolerant: an outer `runCatching` degrades a wholly corrupt value to an empty list, while an inner per-entry `runCatching` skips a single corrupted slot (with a warning log) instead of discarding the entire config list.

Runtime consumption of time-slot configs is snapshot-based: `PlayerRuntime` caches configs and emotion tags into `@Volatile` fields at startup and exposes `refreshMoodSlots()` (invoked via `MoodTimeSlotViewModel.onConfigsChanged` after save/delete), and `PlayerRandomQueueFacade` evaluates the active slot on each random draw to filter the candidate pool.

`EmotionFailureStore` (the `emotion_failures` DataStore) persists emotion-analysis failures in one key `emotion_failures` as a JSONObject keyed by songId with `{reason, failedAt, attempts}`; `record` read-modify-writes in one transaction accumulating `attempts` and overwriting `reason`/`failedAt` with the latest, and parsing skips corrupted entries.

`EmotionScanWorker` consumes failure records: songs with `attempts >= MAX_ATTEMPTS (3)` are excluded from automatic retry so periodic scans do not spin on broken files (manual retry goes through `clearForRetry`, which clears records and re-enqueues), and a successful analysis clears the record via `clear(songId)`.

The periodic emotion scan is scheduled once per app start by `EmotionScanScheduler.schedule` from `MelodyApplication.onCreate`: a unique periodic WorkManager job (`emotion_periodic_scan`, KEEP policy) every 6 hours with charging + battery-not-low constraints and a 30-minute initial delay, ≤40 songs per pass.

Several `:data` repositories bridge persistence with synchronous domain contracts via `runBlocking(Dispatchers.IO)`: `SongEmotionsRepository` (all methods), `PlayStatsRepository`, `QuickSkipSongsRepository`, the `currentXxx()`/`setXxxBlocking()` methods of `PlayerSettingsRepository`, and `PlaybackStateStore`'s save/restore/clear.

The runBlocking(IO) bridge imposes a caller-side thread contract: these methods must not be called on the main thread. Reference patterns are `AppMediaMetadataViewModel.saveEmotionCorrection` wrapping corrections in `withContext(Dispatchers.Default)`, `MoodTimeSlotViewModel.loadStats` doing a one-shot `withContext(Dispatchers.IO)` snapshot for the blocking `songEmotionRepository.getAll`, and `PlayerPersistenceGraph` running the blocking restore read on a `dispatchers.io` coroutine.

Backup/privacy exclusions are a release checklist item: `backup_rules.xml` (`full-backup-content`) and `data_extraction_rules.xml` (`cloud-backup` and `device-transfer`) must both exclude the legacy SharedPreferences (`music_player_prefs.xml`, `play_stats_prefs.xml`, `quick_skip_songs_prefs.xml`), the full Room family (`melody.db`, `-journal`, `-shm`, `-wal`), the two DataStore files (`player_settings.preferences_pb`, `playback_state.preferences_pb`), and the album-art caches; `verifyProductArchitecture` fails the build if any entry is missing.

The DataStore-versus-Room selection rule applied in this codebase: only small, non-relational state goes to DataStore — both `TimeSlotConfigStore` and `EmotionFailureStore` explicitly document 'no Room schema change' as the rationale for JSON-in-DataStore storage, while anything relational or aggregate (library, playlists, stats, emotions) lives in Room.

Persistence has a JVM regression floor: `PlaybackStateStoreTest` (round trip, unavailable-song filtering, infinite-play state, empty-session keep semantics, currentSongId correction, legacy fallback + clear-on-save), `PlaybackStateSnapshotSerializerTest` (round trip, corrupt JSON, missing currentIndex, defaults), `SharedPreferencesLegacyJsonMigrationTest`, `PlaylistResumeDataStoreTest`, and `PlayerSettingsRepositoryTest` lock the behaviors this page documents; changes to these paths must keep those tests green.
